title: Paresh Rawal Walked Away From 'Hera Pheri 3.' He Returned His ₹11 Lakh Signing Fee With 15 Percent Interest. The Franchise May Never Recover.
excerpt: A ₹15 crore payment dispute, a clause that would have made Rawal wait two years for his money, and a legal threat from Akshay Kumar's team. The most beloved comedy franchise in NRI living rooms is in serious trouble.
body:
There are exactly three words every Indian who grew up in the 2000s can finish: "Aye Baburao..." And the man who made Baburao Ganpatrao Apte into a cultural institution has reportedly walked away from *Hera Pheri 3*.

Paresh Rawal — one of the finest character actors in Indian cinema, and the undisputed comic anchor of the *Hera Pheri* franchise — has exited the long-awaited third film. He's returned his signing fee of ₹11 lakh along with 15% yearly interest and a goodwill amount, effectively severing his contractual ties with the production.

The franchise, which also stars Akshay Kumar and Suniel Shetty, may not survive this.

## The Money Problem

The dispute is fundamentally about payment structure. Rawal's total fee was locked at ₹15 crore. But the contract specified that the balance — ₹14.89 crore — would be paid only one month after the film's theatrical release.

Here's the problem: the film's principal photography hasn't even started. Shooting is scheduled for next year, which means *Hera Pheri 3* is unlikely to hit theatres before late 2026 or 2027. That's a two-year wait for the vast majority of the actor's fee.

A source close to the production told media outlets: "Paresh had reservations about this clause. In short, he would have had to wait for nearly two years to get the rest of his acting fees."

For a senior actor of Rawal's stature — one who has been delivering consistently for four decades — the terms were reportedly unacceptable.

## Legal Escalation

Rawal's exit didn't go quietly. Reports suggest that Akshay Kumar's production team initiated legal action, arguing that early preparation, logistics, and promotional groundwork had already begun. The sudden departure, they claimed, caused financial losses.

The counter-argument from Rawal's side is equally straightforward: a contract that delays 99.3% of your payment until after a film's uncertain release date isn't a contract — it's a gamble.

Meanwhile, producer Firoz Nadiadwala, who holds the franchise rights, faces a separate legal dispute with Vijay Kumar over the property itself. The layers of conflict make *Hera Pheri 3* look less like a film in production and more like a case study in Bollywood's contract dysfunction.

## Why NRIs Should Be Alarmed

No Bollywood franchise has deeper roots in the Indian diaspora than *Hera Pheri*. The 2000 original and its 2006 sequel aren't just comedies — they're cultural infrastructure. "25 din mein paisa double" is a financial philosophy in NRI WhatsApp groups. Baburao's deadpan delivery is the default reaction GIF in South Asian group chats from London to Los Angeles.

When reports surfaced in 2022 that the original trio would reunite under Priyadarshan's direction, the excitement in diaspora communities was palpable. WhatsApp forwards. Instagram edits. Reddit threads debating whether anything could recapture the original's magic.

If Paresh Rawal doesn't return, that excitement turns to ash. You can recast many roles in Bollywood. You cannot recast Baburao. The character is inseparable from the actor — his timing, his expressions, his ability to make a line about "upar wala" feel like scripture.

## Is There Hope?

Some later reports suggest that discussions between Rawal and the makers may have resumed. A few entertainment portals claimed the issues were "eventually resolved" and Rawal could return.

But there's been no detailed official confirmation. No statement from Rawal. No statement from Nadiadwala. No statement from Akshay Kumar, who earlier expressed uncertainty about the project's future.

Priyadarshan — the director who made the original *Hera Pheri* a classic and is attached to direct the third — has also stayed silent publicly. His involvement was supposed to be the guarantee that the sequel wouldn't be a pale imitation. Without Rawal, that guarantee is meaningless.

## The Bigger Picture

Bollywood has a contract problem. Payment disputes between actors and producers are endemic, but they usually play out behind closed doors. The *Hera Pheri 3* situation has gone public precisely because the franchise is too beloved for anyone to look away.

For fans in the diaspora — the ones who grew up watching Raju, Shyam, and Baburao on pirated DVDs and now stream Bollywood on JioHotstar — this isn't just industry gossip. It's the potential death of a reunion they've waited 20 years for.

The only winning move for the makers is to fix the contract, pay the man what he's worth, and make the film. Anything else is, to quote the franchise itself, "devi prasad" — a problem that just keeps getting worse the longer you ignore it.
nri_angle: Hera Pheri is arguably the single most-quoted Bollywood franchise in the Indian diaspora. Baburao Ganpatrao Apte memes are a shared language from New Jersey to Brampton. If Paresh Rawal doesn't return, the film loses its soul — and NRI audiences lose a piece of their childhood.
author: Diaspora Desk
